profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a for-profit public company founded in 1993, headquartered in Santa Clara, California, and traded as NVDA. Its CIK is 0001045810, and its latest 10-K reports revenue of $215938000000 for the period ending 2026-01-25. NVIDIA has 281 California law exposure entries and no recorded cases. Its AI products include NVIDIA Nemotron, an enterprise LLM family with synthetic data generation, GPU-optimized, self-hosted options, and NVIDIA NIM, inference microservices for deploying foundation models with enterprise GPU optimization and self-hosted options.

NVIDIA describes the Nemotron family as highly efficient, multimodal, open AI models built for long-running, self-evolving agents, with transparent training data and support for NVIDIA RTX PRO and NVIDIA DGX Spark. The site mentions NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for specialized tasks and NeMo Switchyard for routing steps to the right model. Bryan Catanzaro, NVIDIA's VP of applied deep learning research, is quoted on the vision behind Nemotron and open technologies. The Nemotron family includes Nemotron Speech models for ASR, TTS, and neural machine translation, and Nemotron Retriever models for document understanding, embeddings, and rank-ordering. NVIDIA says the models excel in agentic AI tasks including reasoning, multimodal vision, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), speech, and safety.

NVIDIA publishes training datasets, techniques, and model weights under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which the company describes as permissive, allowing use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without crediting NVIDIA. Nemotron models are also offered as NVIDIA NIM microservices, which require an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license and can be downloaded from build.nvidia.com. NVIDIA lists NVIDIA Dynamo, TensorRT-LLM, and NIM as tools to run Nemotron models at scale, alongside open-source libraries SGLang and vLLM. The site also points to NVIDIA NeMo for custom agentic AI and NVIDIA Blueprints for customizable reference workflows, and says NVIDIA works with partners including model builders and AI-native companies to improve Nemotron models.
